issues.detail: The Greek 'εκ του εμου' (from mine) refers to the Father's possessions/things ('οσα εχει ο πατηρ'), but the Vietnamese 'từ điều thuộc về ta' (from what belongs to me) is slightly ambiguous. More importantly, the Greek 'ληψεται' (will take/receive) in this context implies a movement of possession from the Father's realm to the Son's for the purpose of revelation, whereas the Vietnamese phrasing suggests taking from the Son's own possessions.
